title: The Borrowed Shadow
narration: My shadow entered the house five seconds before I did. It pointed me toward hidden speakers and cameras while footsteps moved upstairs. Police found my landlord in the attic with recordings and copied keys; he claimed he projected the shadow to frighten me away. But his projector faced the wrong wall. Security footage showed a dark shape rising behind him. The silence felt deliberate, as though someone nearby was waiting for me to understand the trap before moving again. For several seconds I could hear nothing except my breathing and the small ordinary sounds around me. Every explanation I tried made the details worse, because each clue had been placed where I alone would find it. My shadow had not entered to scare me—it had gone inside to lock him in.
